sectors.name: Petroleum Refining, Petrochemicals & Energy Security
sectors.priorityNote: Dakshina Kannada is Karnataka's refining and petrochemical base. Its aromatics complex in the Mangalore SEZ (formerly ONGC Mangalore Petrochemicals, 442 acres, Rs 7,500 crore) is rated at 914 KTPA para-xylene and 283 KTPA benzene. The district also holds a 1.5 MMT underground strategic crude reserve at Permude, and in July 2026 ONGC's board approved a further 1.75 MT strategic petroleum reserve at Mangaluru as a project of national importance. Invest Karnataka records MRPL's investment in the district at Rs 25,409 crore. MRPL spent Rs 2,044 crore on capex and long-term investment in 2025-26 (Rs 1,154 crore in 2024-25).

sectors.name: Port, Shipping & Logistics
sectors.priorityNote: New Mangalore Port, Karnataka's only major port, handled a record 50.04 MMT of cargo in 2025-26, up 8.8% from 46.01 MMT, and 1,79,594 TEUs of containers. It is India's largest coffee exporter and second-largest LPG importer, 92% mechanised and 100% solar powered, with usable capacity of 74 MMT and a goal of 100 MMT by 2047. At its Golden Jubilee in November 2025, 16 infrastructure and 113 CSR projects worth Rs 1,500 crore were inaugurated or begun, including a 150-bed PPP hospital, and NMPA signed Rs 52,000 crore of MoUs at India Maritime Week 2025. In March 2026 the Ministry approved a Rs 438.29 crore PPP redevelopment of Berth No. 9 (draft 10.5 m to 14 m, 10.90 MTPA, vessels up to 2 lakh DWT). Cargo beat the ministry's 48.5 MMT target; Berth No. 13 is proposed for captive users and Berth No. 17 is to be tendered. The Rs 196.51 crore Kulai fishing harbour is listed by Sagarmala as under implementation. In 2024-25 NMPA earned an operating income of Rs 921.36 crore, an operating surplus of Rs 611 crore and profit after tax of Rs 420.57 crore.

dc.headline: Dakshina Kannada is Karnataka's 2nd-largest district economy (GDDP Rs 1,54,509 cr) with the 2nd-highest per-capita income (Rs 6.26 lakh) and the state's highest industry share (37.4%). The agenda is lending more of its large deposit base locally (CD 70.04%), diversifying beyond arecanut and beedi livelihoods, and building on port and refinery-led industry.

industrial.headline: Karnataka's most industrial district (industry 37.4% of GDDP): MRPL's refinery, New Mangalore Port (50.04 MMT in 2025-26), fertiliser and chemical units at Panambur and Baikampady, and 99,854 Udyam MSMEs. The Ganjimutt Plastic Park opens downstream opportunities; estate-wise land data needs refreshing.

revenue.headline: Land for industry sits in older KIADB estates (Baikampady, Canara, EPIP, IT SEZ) and the new Ganjimutt Plastic Park. With groundwater Safe in every taluk, land-water conflicts are limited; the priority is clean, current estate-wise land records.

actions.title: Ganjimutt Plastic Park (plot allotment opened Apr 2026)
Mangaluru Smart City: 98 of 105 projects completed

agriculture.headline: A high-rainfall (4,006 mm normal), well-irrigated plantation district: arecanut (about 99,000 ha), coconut, cashew and cocoa, with marine fisheries as its One District One Product (3.45 lakh MT). Holdings are small (63% under 1 ha) and incomes depend heavily on arecanut.

water.headline: Water is a strength: extraction is 45.71% of extractable groundwater (state 66.49%) and all nine taluks are Safe (GWRA 2025). Irrigation is about 84% well-fed with no canal command, so the task is recharge and efficient use in Sulya and Bantwal.

health.headline: A major healthcare hub: 2,880 hospitals, 23,234 beds and 5,059 doctors (DES 2024-25), with PHCs (77) and sub-centres (430) meeting IPHS norms. Community health centres (7, 2010-11 count) are below the norm and need a fresh audit.

education.headline: Literacy is 88.57% (3rd in Karnataka; male 93.13%, female 84.13%) and the district ranks 2nd on HDI, with Mangalore the top taluk. The education index (0.595) is the lowest of its three HDI components, driven by mean years of schooling (0.479).

minister.headline: Dakshina Kannada: 20.9 lakh people (Census 2011), Karnataka's 2nd-largest district economy (Rs 1,54,509 cr) and 2nd-highest per-capita income (Rs 6.26 lakh), with the state's highest industry share (37.4%), a record-cargo port and groundwater Safe in all nine taluks. The gaps are local credit deployment (CD 70.04%) and livelihoods tied to arecanut and beedi rolling.

digitalEconomy.storiesSub: Cluster companies that grew into global players.

stories.title: Novigo Solutions - Mangaluru
stories.subtitle: Acquired for up to Rs 950 Cr after 44% annual growth
stories.body: Founded in Mangaluru in 2013, Novigo grew revenue 44% a year to Rs 264 Cr in FY25 at a 25% EBITDA margin. Blackstone-backed R Systems bought it in 2025 for Rs 400 Cr upfront plus performance-linked stock, valued at Rs 950 Cr by KDEM. 56% of its people work in Mangaluru.
stories.significance: A Mangaluru-born company scaled to Rs 264 Cr and delivered a landmark exit
stories.source: R Systems International disclosure to BSE, 21 Aug 2025; Draft Mangaluru Cluster Vision Document 2025, p43

series.label: Revenue (Rs Cr)
series.note: All three years as disclosed in R Systems' filing: Rs 101.7 Cr, Rs 199.0 Cr and Rs 264.4 Cr (FY25 provisional).

stories.title: Robosoft Technologies - Udupi
stories.subtitle: Built from Udupi, with Apple as its first customer
stories.body: Founded in 1996 with Apple as its first customer, Robosoft grew from Udupi into a global digital product company. Net sales rose from Rs 75 Cr (FY19) to Rs 184 Cr (FY21), and Japan's TechnoPro Holdings acquired it for Rs 805 Cr in 2021.

series.label: Net sales (Rs Cr)
series.note: All three years as disclosed by the acquirer.

stories.title: Niveus Solutions - Udupi
stories.subtitle: Udupi's award-winning Google Cloud partner
stories.body: Udupi-based Niveus won Google Cloud's 2024 Breakthrough Partner of the Year (APAC) and Services Partner of the Year (India). NTT DATA acquired it in February 2025, adding 1,000+ Google Cloud engineers.
stories.significance: An Udupi company became a top Google Cloud partner and joined NTT DATA, a $30B+ global IT group

stories.heroLabel: EG A/S team in Mangaluru, its largest GCC outside Europe

stories.subtitle: Global companies choosing Mangaluru for their global teams
stories.body: Denmark's EG A/S built an 850-member team in Mangaluru in two years, its largest GCC outside Europe. Bose Professional opened its first R&D centre outside Massachusetts here, projected to reach 100 people. KDEM counts 15+ GCCs in the cluster.
stories.significance: Global companies are choosing Mangaluru for capability and R&D centres
